claims: Cinco de Mayo is celebrated annually on May 5.
Cinco de Mayo commemorates the Mexican army's unexpected 1862 victory over France at the Battle of Puebla.
Mexican Independence Day is celebrated on September 16.
Cinco de Mayo is not Mexican Independence Day.
Mexican Independence Day marks the beginning of the war of independence against Spain in 1810.
On May 5, 1862, a smaller, poorly equipped Mexican army led by General Ignacio Zaragoza defeated a larger, elite French army in Puebla, Mexico.
Cinco de Mayo is not a major national holiday in Mexico except in Puebla.
Cinco de Mayo became a popular celebration of heritage in the U.S. during the 1960s Chicano movement.
Cinco de Mayo is primarily celebrated in the state of Puebla in Mexico with parades, speeches, and massive reenactments of the battle.
Traditional foods include mole poblano, tacos, and guacamole.
In 2026, Cinco de Mayo falls on a Tuesday.
